name: Councilman Millstipe
summary: Darkshire's council grows bitter as Stormwind overrides its judgment. Councilman Millstipe lives in the town hall and wants justice for Duskwood's people.

sections.title: Justice Denied by Stormwind
sections.body: Darkshire faces undead and attacks from ferocious beasts, while its council struggles against Stormwind City's bureaucracy. Councilman Millstipe reflects the town's growing bitterness toward the crown. The notorious grave robber Dextren Ward was caught selling freshly dug corpses to the necromancer Morbent Fel. Darkshire's leaders sentenced Ward to death, but Stormwind's House of Nobles commuted the execution and locked him away in the Stormwind Stockade.

sections.title: A Message to the Nobles
sections.body: Councilman Millstipe believes Stormwind's politicians have put Duskwood's safety and justice aside. He discreetly directs adventurers to kill Dextren Ward in his Stockade cell. The order defies the House of Nobles and warns that, if Stormwind will not protect Duskwood's people, they will take justice into their own hands.

faq.q: Where can Councilman Millstipe be found?
faq.answer: Councilman Millstipe can be found inside Darkshire's town hall, in eastern Duskwood.

faq.q: Why does Millstipe want Dextren Ward dead?
faq.answer: Dextren Ward was a grave robber who dug up Duskwood's dead and sold them to the necromancer Morbent Fel. Lord Ebonlocke sentenced him to be beheaded, but Stormwind's House of Nobles spared him and sent him to the Stockade.

faq.q: What is Millstipe's grievance with Stormwind?
faq.answer: Millstipe believes Stormwind has abandoned Duskwood while interfering with its local justice. The House of Nobles overturned Darkshire's death sentence for Dextren Ward, leaving the settlement feeling ignored and unprotected by the throne.

faq.q: Does Millstipe have any known family?
faq.answer: No family of Councilman Millstipe is known.

angles.text: Millstipe shows the political divide between Stormwind's sheltered nobility and Duskwood's desperate frontier settlements, which receive little aid and face heavy-handed interference from the capital.
For a rogue willing to enter the heavily guarded Stockade and carry out an unsanctioned political execution, Millstipe offers work that defies the House of Nobles.
